source.title: Hurricane causes resource and pollination limitation of fruit set in a bird-pollinated shrub

design: Before/after natural experiment on San Salvador Island across a pre-hurricane season, a mild-hurricane season, and the season after severe Hurricane Lili, with pollinator abundance, nectar removal, stigma pollen receipt and fruit-set limitation measured in Pavonia bahamensis.

source_native_results.pollination_limitation_after_lili: fruit set was reduced an additional 74% by pollination limitation after separating resource limitation
source_native_results.pollinator_change: Bananaquit and Bahama Woodstar flower visitation collapsed; Bananaquit populations were decimated and bird visits became rare
source_native_results.pollen_receipt: 98% of stigmas received pollen before the hurricanes versus 51% of flowers receiving no pollen after Hurricane Lili
source_native_results.replacement: no compensatory pollination by other bird species or insects was detected

observed_chain: hurricane-driven bird-pollinator decline -> near-loss of nectar removal and pollen receipt -> strong pollination limitation -> fruit-set collapse
claim_boundary: The hurricane also caused direct resource limitation, which the source explicitly measured; the strict pollination claim is therefore the additional pollination-limitation component, not attribution of the whole fruit-set decline to pollinator loss. This validates qualitative propagation, not the ABM trait-position mechanism.
